name: Brand Concepts Ltd
title: Brand Concepts Ltd - 543442 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Q1 FY27 revenue up ~11% but PBT loss widened; management says PC plant at 80%+ utilisation, PP plant ramping, and sees inventory cut to ~130 days, with capex pause for two years.

summary.headline: Brand Concepts Q1 FY27 revenue grew ~11% and EBITDA rose, but PBT loss widened; management expects growth to resume from October.
summary.overview: Management said revenue grew almost 11% YoY and EBITDA grew on lower overheads, while the PBT loss widened marginally on higher depreciation, interest and operating investments. Primary billing took a dent from an e-commerce SKU realignment and channel consolidation, though secondary sales were said to be strong and market share was claimed to be intact. Retail tail-clipping continued: about 75-80% of the store consolidation is done, with completion targeted by September. The new hard-luggage and PP plants are ramping, with the PC unit at 80%+ utilisation on internal consumption only.

segments.name: Luggage / travel gear
segments.commentary: Management said luggage grew low single digits YoY in Q1; travel care overall was negative, driven by backpack SKU consolidation. Pricing pressure from new D2C entrants persists.

segments.name: E-commerce
segments.commentary: Primary billing hit by high-volume SKU realignment; management expects e-commerce to be back on track from August 2026. Secondary sales described as strong.

segments.name: Modern trade / EBO retail
segments.commentary: EBO business was about 10% of overall business. Multiple BAGLINE stores closed as unprofitable; nine further stores on notice per analyst question. Shoppers Stop secondary growth upwards of 12% per management.

segments.name: Tommy Hilfiger
segments.commentary: Overall flattish; volume down low single digits but ASP up. Licence renewal from international counterparty is pending paperwork; 10-year business plan and royalty terms said to be closed, royalty 'same'.

segments.name: Benetton
segments.commentary: Primary de-growth; earlier strategies failed. Management pivoting to a sharp-price e-commerce line and new offline styles launching next month, with CSD entry planned.

segments.name: New brands (Off-White, Superdry, Juicy)
segments.commentary: Off-White launched about April 2026 with Bangalore and Delhi stores; plan of five stores in total, four done. Superdry luggage not yet launched; Juicy FY26 revenue INR12 crore, FY27 target INR20-22 crore.

segments.name: Manufacturing (PC / PP)
segments.commentary: PC unit at 80%+ utilisation, internal only. PP plant trials done with production ramp; combined capacity ~50,000 pieces/month, with ~20,000 currently and ~40,000 targeted by October-November.

guidance_outlook: Management expects company-level growth to resume from October 2026, with consolidation ~80% complete and to finish by September.
Phase three (operating leverage) expected in about 1.5 years, per management's conservative view.
Management expects EBITDA margins to keep showing a healthy trend and FY27 to be a good year.
No new debt planned beyond the government scheme already availed; FY27 end expected to be the debt peak; long-term aim of a debt-free company in about 5 years.
No major capex for the next two years unless a large order pipeline emerges; existing building can host up to four lines, with ~INR10 crore needed for another 50,000 capacity.
Apparel in-house for Juicy targeted at ~70-75% by Q3 FY28; PP launch from October could add ~20,000 pieces/month at ~INR1,500 ASP.
Management said it is too early to quantify PP revenue contribution for the festive season.
Management is not planning new Off-White stores beyond the five planned; Juicy to add a couple of stores then slow down over the next year.
capex_capacity: PC unit ~25,000 pieces/month capacity, at 80%+ utilisation on internal consumption only; no external clients yet.
PP plant (one machine) trials complete, targeting 75-80% utilisation within about two months; moulds to arrive by end-September with production from October.
Combined ~50,000 pieces/month capacity; ~20,000 running now, ~40,000 targeted by October or November.
Plant reportedly profitable at 20,000 pieces/month vs earlier breakeven estimate of 30,000-35,000; management estimates ~11-13% EBITDA at plant level at 40,000 pieces, not yet verified.
Building can house four lines of 25,000 each (100,000 pieces/month); ~INR10 crore of machinery adds ~50,000 capacity.
Third-party manufacturing planned; Samsonite group is a backpack client for Go-To-Wander bags. Management aims for no more than 50% captive consumption of installed capacity.
demand_pricing: Pricing pressure persists from new D2C and premium entrants in travel gear; management says it will not chase unhealthy discounts.
Management claims no market share lost at company level; some volume decline at Tommy Hilfiger offset by higher ASP.
Travel demand reduced; raw material costs up due to war-related conditions, per management.
Management said premium-end consumers remain resilient, citing top-selling INR27,000-32,000 luggage sets at Tommy Hilfiger.
Management declined to give same-store sales growth now; will consider SSSG metrics in a couple of quarters.
Seasonality shift: Q2 now bigger than Q1 due to festive-season primary orders, and expected to continue this year.

qa_highlights.question: Tommy Hilfiger licence status and terms?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the international licence renewal is delayed but paperwork-only; the 10-year business plan, royalty and figures are closed, with royalty unchanged.

qa_highlights.question: Manufacturing utilisation, benefit and pass-through?
qa_highlights.answer: PC at 80%+ utilisation on internal consumption; PP ramping. Management said most of the plant margin benefit is being passed to consumers via pricing to stay relevant.

qa_highlights.question: Cash flow, funding and capital plans?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said cash is not a constraint; inventory fell ~INR5 crore, Q1 negative is temporary and INR20 crore promoter capital was committed (INR15 crore in). No new debt planned.

qa_highlights.question: When does consolidation end and when does growth return?
qa_highlights.answer: Consolidation about 75-80% done; stores to exit by September, e-commerce reset this month, and growth expected back from October.

qa_highlights.question: Store closure impact and INR1,000 crore target?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said reported figures are post-closures, EBO is ~10% of business, and the INR1,000 crore target over 4-5 years remains on track.

qa_highlights.question: Inventory days and Benetton plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Inventory INR123 crore at June-end, about 130 days per management. Benetton had failed strategies; pivoted to e-commerce price-led line and new offline styles next month.

financial_highlights.value: Growth described as healthy, in line with revenue; no absolute figure given
INR123 crore at June-end vs INR128 crore at March-end (~130 inventory days per management)
~INR4 crore in Q1; ~INR16 crore expected for FY27
financial_highlights.change: Marginally higher YoY on full-year manufacturing

financial_highlights.value: INR20 crore committed, INR15 crore already in system
INR12 crore in FY26; target INR20-22 crore in FY27
